claims.text: The initially synthesized WTaCrVHf refractory high-entropy alloy is nanocrystalline.
The initially synthesized alloy has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Controlled annealing following cold work can induce fine refractory carbide or intermetallic precipitates at grain boundaries and within grains.
The proposed treatment will produce a dual-phase microstructure comprising a refined nanocrystalline matrix and evenly dispersed nanoprecipitates.
The nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation glide and provide precipitation strengthening.
The refined grain structure will increase strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Combining precipitation strengthening and grain-boundary strengthening will increase yield and tensile strength.
The refractory and stable nature of the proposed phases will prevent grain growth and undesirable phase transformations during high-temperature or irradiation exposure.
The treated alloy will have statistically significantly higher strength than the as-synthesized alloy.
The treated alloy will retain its nanocrystalline microstructure and resist grain coarsening or phase instability during thermal and irradiation exposure.
The as-synthesized WTaCrVHf alloy has high thermal stability.
The as-synthesized WTaCrVHf alloy is resistant to irradiation.
The nanocrystalline WTaCrVHf alloy undergoes grain refinement under heavy-ion irradiation.
The nanocrystalline WTaCrVHf alloy resists dual-beam irradiation and helium implantation through low defect generation and evolution and no detectable grain growth.
The proposed benefits should persist at service temperatures above 1000 degrees Celsius.
The proposed benefits should persist under heavy-ion or dual-beam irradiation with helium implantation.
The intervention will be effective if temperature, duration, and strain are optimized to form nanoprecipitates without excessive grain growth or adverse phase transformations.
